.

.

.
Vote suppression has many levels.
.
People are discouraged from registering;

Low information voters are encouraged to waste their votes, or to behave irresponsibly or short-sightedly.
.

.
At the end of the day, in the era of abuse of big data and narrow-cast online browser tracking and targeting, nominal turnout is a weak trend-revealing indicator, because it is a secondary or derivative indicator.
.
Absolute turnout, by contrast, is virtually always determinative.

Wolf Eagle, Dall sheep rams in the Chugach Mountains don't grow full-curl horns until age 7 or 8. Most rams don't live much longer than that. After the breeding season, which is in early winter, a large ram's fat reserves are seriously depleted and during a harsh winter the older rams are among the first to die of starvation and other natural causes. There are several ways to limit the number of sheep shot during a hunting season; however, one of the best is to restrict the harvest to full-curl sheep because they are a very small segment of the total population, they are the sex-age group most likely to die overwinter and, yes, some hunters like to hang a trophy on the wall. If you can come up with a fairer way to limit the harvest, let me know. Also, Dall sheep are among the tastiest of wild creatures and responsible hunters (i.e., most hunters) carry all the meat off the mountain and are happy to have it.

Colorado's law goes much further - saying that you only need to have a reasonable belief that the intruder MIGHT USE ANY PHYSICAL FORCE, NO MATTER HOW SLIGHT. The freehold mineral titles are not as attractive as Crown leases at the moment.  The Crown leases, I understand, delay the royalty payment until drilling costs are recovered.  Royalty on a freehold lease starts with the first dollar of production.  
There is a freehold mineral tax (FMT) on productive wells which works out to about 5% of net royalty.  (Basic exemption for marginal wells so the resource is extracted rather than abandoned).   If the oil and gas company defaults on the payment of the surface lease for the well site, the farmer can apply to the Alberta government to receive payment in lieu.  The FMT is assessed on the owner, not on the well operator.  If a company chooses not to pay the tax, the freeholder pays or forfeits title. 
This FMT does not apply to Crown leases.  Freehold mineral owners may watch their resource drained away from wells on crown leases without any compensation as the Crown royalty rate is usually lower than freehold royalty plus FMT.

If Portland isn't happy with this liability arrangement, it'll have to ante up to cover the operator's insurance burden.

Bottom line is that bike-sharing stands to make Portland's streets safer and users trimmer. Helmets or not, it'll be a net benefit for Portlanders' health.

The issue is when organizations unilaterally change those rules, then yes it is a big problem. However, if the rules are stated clearly (rather than in fine print), that it's either use it or lose it after 1 year - then it is completely legitimate.

I always find the Star Wars/Star Trek debate funny because they seem so different to me that I have a hard time understanding how the two can be compared. Star Wars, on the other hand, was written as a series of movies with a far-reaching storyline. Star Trek is meant to be set in our own future, complete with our history and built upon our understanding of the real universe. Star Wars, however, exists "a long time ago, in a galaxy far, far away." That opens SW up to potentially involve elements that would be too fantastical in a universe based on our own, no matter how futuristic. There is a difference between pain and suffering, and this is part of the confusion over pain control. Pain is the actual physical sensation, and certainly can be excruciating, which is what narcotics are for. Suffering includes pain, but also includes all the emotional turmoil that surrounds it. So someone who has fibromyalgia, for example, may also experience depression because of loss of independence or inability to work, anxiety related to inability to accept the diagnosis, thinking perhaps that the pain is due to undiagnosed cancer, or frustration at friends or family who may not seem to appreciate the sufferer's distress. None of the latter can be helped by narcotics, but if the only question the health practitioner asks is "do you have pain?" the answer will always be "yes", and the danger is that the dose of pain medication will continue to be increased even although that will only add to the individual's problems rather than relieving them.
